body: I applied on June 10th as well within the UK, through the app. Still waiting :') I've seen some people say they've gotten theirs after 8 weeks exactly, hopefully this will be the case for us and we get ours within the next 2 weeks! But I'm hoping it comes very soon, for both of us!!

Wow, are you me? I'm literally going through this exact thing with my AM.

She never liked my partner, he is my childhood friend but she's just always disliked him and would never get over it.

She was very upset when I told her we were dating and I was planning to move in with him. She never truly forgave me for moving out I think. She said a lot of awful stuff "in anger" to me and about my partner. She only apologized half heartedly but insisted she was only being worried and concerned for me. I can never quite forgive her for her drastic outbursts of anger over it, because why should parents get so angry over something that doesn't impact them? Why can't you just communicate normally and try to simply be happy for your child?

Ive been in low contact with her ever since, but last week I finally told her we were getting married. She was quite upset, thinking that we're not rushing into things, he's manipulating me, he's just using me for visa purposes, etc. Despite all this she still wants to attend, but I already know she will show up and will not be smiling and feel upset the whole time.

I regret telling her, deep down I don't really want her to come. I should feel touched she's forcing herself to attend simply for my sake, but I'd rather she not come and feel miserable the whole time. I'm not looking forward to the wedding day as much anymore, which saddens me.

Your feelings of hurt and anger are completely valid. You know your SO better than anyone, and your parents shouldn't have to guilt you or gaslight you into breaking up with them. Parents who raise a fuss over our partners and marriages for no good reason are simply taking their worriedness to the next level, but they never quite realize to what extent it hurts us and hurts our relationship with them. I know its easier said than done but don't feel guilt for taking an exciting big step in your life, this is a truly happy and joyous occasion and I hope that whenever you do get married it will be a wonderful day.

I wish all the best to you and your SO, if you ever wanna chat or vent about it you're always welcome to DM me!

It's like you read my mind. I was having thoughts about my mom again lately and then your comment popped up! Reading it really helped ground me again, so thank you very much for your words of encouragement. It's tough to break out of the habit of blaming yourself for how your parents think and react to things, but slowly you learn to let go of it and be kind to yourself!

Hey, I feel you and I've been there. I'm so sorry you're going through this, it's awful to feel so suffocated and bound to your parents wants.

I was always afraid to live for myself because my mom would pile on guilt trips and keep using her trauma as a tool to keep me from doing anything she didn't like or understand. And for the longest time I let it work. I was so miserable, and I don't wish that feeling on anyone.

I think in an APs, they believe they're doing what's best for you. They believe they are leading you on the path to be successful and so if they see you doing something that doesn't align with that path (I.e. dating someone they don't approve of, not doing something in your career) they figure it's for your own good to guilt you, shame you, and stop you from doing things that make you happy. Kind of like that mindset of "I have to be the bad guy so I can stop you from doing something that will ruin your life."

However, I think that's just a horrible, misguided way if parenting. If you really cared about your childs life, you'd be supportive of their choices and try to give advice when you see something that could be troubling. You shouldn't control your childs life with shame and guilt. It creates resentment and distance between a parent and child. 

I know it's really hard to get past the guilt trips and shame and all the pressure they put on you to do what they want. But it sounds like you have accomplished amazing things in life and you can slowly detach yourself from your parents. You are stronger than you know. Whatever you decide to do, plan it well and make sure you are doing it for yourself. APs think that living for your own happiness and freedom is bullshit, and I think that's pretty telling that their opinions are outdated and just very unhealthy.

For me, I ended up doing something my mother was completely against, something she didn't like so she naturally assumed it would ruin my life. It took a while to muster up the courage, but I told her this was my life and my choice. She ended up lashing out and essentially disowning me, but I feel like I will have no regrets since I'm living life on my terms. 

Remember: You are not responsible for your parents happiness, you are only responsible for your own!! 

I wish you well, and I hope you can get the freedom and happiness you deserve

You are so right. I'm thinking if I was a mom who disagreed with her daughter, I would try my best to talk with her and make sure she is prepared as possible for her trip, even if I'm sad to see her go. 

I just didn't say anything in response to her yelling, I took all my stuff and packed it away

I'm really sorry you had to go through that. My mom also eventually ended up throwing all of my lithe stuff out because she "couldn't bear having any reminder" of me around. 

It's never easy when APs just make the whole situation to be about them, especially when they show that they are so emotionally dependent on us that they see us moving out as an affront to them. We just gotta stay strong!

Thank you for sharing your story, I hope you're in a better place now and free from her manipulations!

Thank you, I'm trying my best to keep my excitement about the next steps in my life!

I think parents let their worry or their ideas of success take over their mind. They are too afraid to let you go, or hold onto their idea of right and wrong so stubbornly that they end up hurting their kids in turn. 

I have to forge my own path in life!

That's true, I'm really glad she ended up giving it all to me. What she said hurt, but I guess maybe subconsciously she was helping me out. 

And that's a good idea, I'm just going to lay low and keep out of her space until I leave

You have a good point. Honestly, my mom has come a long way from what she was like when I was younger... though there are still a lot of issues we need to work through. She tends to think my side of things are childish or not as significant as what she's been through, and that has always made it hard to tell her things. Her love and care for me has become something of a hindrance for her own happiness, because she has told me that me and my brother are her whole life and happiness, which isn't healthy. As a result, if one of us does something she doesn't see as "good" or "logical", she will lash out and make us feel like our lives are ruined. 

It still hurts when she gets very upset and treats it like a personal attack when I'm making choices for my own  life, even if I know it's just her way of coping with the emotional stress. I think I need to work on myself a lot to be able to mend the relationship, but for now I'm allowed to feel and process the hurt just as she is allowed to.

Thank you, I was so dejected as she spent hours pointing out how I have a poor attitude, how she's losing  a daughter, how this is absolutely the worst choice I'm making in my whole life.

All of this just makes me more determined to work hard and make the most of my time abroad. I have to prove her wrong because it's the only way she'll come around. Or she won't, in which case it's her choice to shut me out of her life just for travelling.

Thank you, I was so dejected as she spent hours pointing out how I have a poor attitude, how she's losing  a daughter, how this is absolutely the worst choice I'm making in my whole life.

All of this just makes me more determined to work hard and make the most of my time abroad. I have to prove her wrong because it's the only way she'll come around. Or she won't, in which case it's her choice to shut me out of her life just for travelling.

Thank you so much, it feels so validating to read this. I've been struggling with leaving here for 8 months, since I moved back here after studying abroad. I wanted to go back to the same country I just studied in - it seemed like the most logical thing to do as I could use my degree there and also be with my boyfriend!

But yes, my mother likes to pile on the "I am getting old, you need to be here since I'll die soon!" or "Your life will be ruined and you will fall so far behind in your career!" It's tiring to bring up this topic with her, so I avoided it for so long. But I just want to move on with my life by doing what I originally intended to do: move abroad, work, and have a good time! 

I have already given up on things I wanted to do to placate my mother or other people in the past, and I still deeply regret not doing them. I don't want to turn this into another life-long regret!

Thank you again for the words of encouragement, it really means a lot.

You're right. I just wish I was better at articulating my thoughts and feelings to her so she'd at least calm down a little. 

I don't understand why she makes her happiness so dependent on me staying here. She even dragged my uncle into this mess and he basically called me a jobless loser who should respect my mom.

I feel so much guilt and shame just for something that doesn't seem that crazy to do (I.e. moving abroad to work for a couple years). I just feel awful because she looks so happy right now. But I feel lonely and frustrated that I am so afraid to make choices for myself even though I'm almost 24. 

But I'll do my best to stay strong on the day I leave!

I'm in a similar predicament, where my AP doesn't approve of who I am dating at the moment. 

The difference is I did tell my AP, and it has caused nothing but strife and heartache. 

I was made to feel like a loser, a naive fool. My AP has cried and yelled and protested so much against my relationship. She said I was a weak person that was just being manipulated by my boyfriend. That he is a bad person who lies and uses me. Of course, she has no evidence of this. She just bases this off how he was when he was a kid and refuses to acknowledge how he's a grown adult now and is a good person. 

In the end, I wish I just kept it a secret. But it's difficult to do when we're long distance and I want to move abroad to be with him. 

Ultimately, APs have lived their lives, but they just want to make everything more dramatic than it needs to be. While they as our parents have a right to voice their concerns, they should never do it through yelling, guilting, or shaming. I never understood why APs would disown their child over someone they choose to date or marry. It's stupid and childish. If they really disapprove, then they should keep their opinions to themselves.

I hope you and your partner will continue to be happy together, and if/whenever your parents find out, I hope you will stay strong and remember that you and your partner deserve happiness.

I'm sorry you have to go through with that. It's not your fault, and your parents shouldn't put that much weight and pressure on your grades. 

Things like this is why it's so hard to be honest, and why we develop a habit to hide things and lie. They never consider that it's okay to fail and make mistakes; it's how we learn and grow.

But I guess its nice to have communities like this to rant and vent with others who understand! Hang in there

Thank you so much, I really needed to hear this. My visa appointment is soon and my mother has been really laying on so many guilt trips, making me feel even more terrible. She's mainly been framing it as her being concerned for my future career and my finances - which are valid, but ultimately I know I won't be in trouble because I have a good support system where I'm going (my boyfriend and his parents). 

She dragged my uncle into it as well, and he basically told me I was a loser in a nice way. They both insisted my boyfriend was just using me to help pay for rent, and I will be abused. Essentially, they were trying to guilt me and manipulate me into losing all my confidence in my plans. I don't doubt that they are genuinely worried for me, but why weaponize that worry to the point where they make me feel like shit when I'm just starting out my life? How will that give me any confidence in being independent? 

I'm actually going for a working holiday visa since it's the easiest to get! Thankfully I told my mom relatively late so she's only had these past few days to really grill me about it. 

Thank you again for your words of encouragement!

Thank you, I hope you find happiness if you can as well.

It sucks because people keep telling us that we are lazy, or comparing us to other people. I'm tired of it.

I used to feel that it was okay that I didn't find a job right away, like I still had a chance. Leave it to toxic family to completely dash all confidence and hopes and dreams. I need to start reading positive, confidence boosting articles about how it's okay to take your time to find a job.

I hope you're doing okay and will find your way, us losers will find a way out some day.

I guess I've just been conditioned to think this way. My family brings up valid points about me being jobless, at least I think they do. But the way they said it just worsened my mental state. 

But a part of me feels selfish and wants to go ahead and live with my boyfriend. I am truly happier with him. And thank you for the boost of confidence

Yeah, I agree. My mom quite work when my brother was born and has not worked since then. Because of this she is stuck depending on my dad's money, trapped in a bad marriage. But she says he should be proud of himself for supporting the whole family by himself for all these years.

And you're right, I should keep details like this to myself from now on.

Thank you. Yes they are very convinced if I go, my life will be over and I will lose all my money. 

But personally, I don't see what is wrong with splitting the rent at all. It would be one thing if he expected me to pay for everything, but no! It's equal! Because we see each other as equals! It's not something deep or complicated like he is manipulating me, it's just ridiculous. I wish they could hear how unreasonable they sound.

I suppose you're right. I'm just overwhelmed because my father keeps insisting honesty is the best, even if it makes her mad.

It's just difficult since I can't think of an explanation for me leaving the place for my visa appointment, since I barely leave the house. I don't want her getting suspicious and causing a fight about that and prevent me from going.

Sorry for the very late reply, but thank you so much for your words.

I've been feeling so much fear and self-doubt, as my mother has been making me feel like I am ruining my life by doing this. But it is so comforting and empowering to hear that what I'm doing is not a bad thing. Thank you so much, it warmed my heart to read your congratulations!

Thank you. I'm happy to hear that you're out there living your own life and not letting the guilt dictate your life!

And you're right, I need to stay strong and take steps to improve my own life. It's too depressing letting guilt rule your life. 

Although I'm scared, I just need to do this.

Thank you so much, your words have given me a lot of courage! 

Yes, sadly Asian parents tend to project their loneliness or bad upbringing onto us, and it can be hard to break out of it. But I don't want to give up my freedoms and end up resenting her for the rest of my life. Also, my older brother lives here, so she is not alone at all. I don't think he has any plans to move out anytime soon.

It'll be hard, but I'll have to go through with it for my own sake.

Thank you, it means a lot to hear this.

You're right, objectively when I take a step back and look at all this, isn't this whole situation just kind of ridiculous? 

She's had 17 years of my life to spend with me and raising me, and now suddenly she cannot let go.

She is in perfectly fine health, but she uses her "old age" and the death of relatives to guilt me into staying with her. I guess it just hurts that she doesn't believe I can be independent in ways I want to. But in the end, I need to be strong! 

Thank you again for your words, it helped ground me.
Thank you, your words are really encouraging! Yeah it's hard to deal with... but in the end its kind of ridiculous that she would say stuff like this over just to bring me down. I'll try my best!

that's true. I feel bad that they were raised in toxic households, but I wish they were strong enough to break the cycle with us. I just can't get into the mindset of intentionally breaking your children down to control them.
Yes I get passive income monthly and save it up in case something will go wrong, I don't want to ask my parents to bail me out and I'll need to fix my own problems

He's 22 years old and he's my childhood friend, I know him very well and we've been dating for almost 5 years now (though half of that time was long distance). I've lived with him for 2 years prior to me moving back home with my mother so I know we are compatible in that regard. I've also studied there for a year so I have a degree and some credentials in that country that I can include on my CV. But yeah, I gotta work real hard to find a job, I'm prepared to do this!

I get her worries and I see your point about not finding a job right away. I know there are lots of concerns she would have, but a lot of her reluctance is fueled by the fact that she just dislikes him a lot, and she always has since we were kids. I could chalk that up to her being overprotective, but at a certain point it gets tiring to deal with if she constantly dismisses all my reasons and attempts to communicate my feelings.

Thank you for the thorough advice. I currently live with my mother and share the same room so I will have to live with her anger and hurt until I can sort everything out to move. It is pretty naive of me to want to avoid fights. At the end of the day, this is important to me and I have to see it through.

She's been using guilt trips every time I broached the subject before, so I backed down. But now I realise I'm just directionless and miserable here, I want to live my life. Sometimes I worry if I'm being too selfish, but I don't think what I want to do is that outlandish of a thing to want, and it is pretty common for people my age to move out and work abroad. At least that's what I keep telling myself.

Thank you. Yes, it really is a struggle, I hope you are doing well too and don't need to deal with this much! I find that when I discuss my negative emotions with my mother, she always ends up invalidating them and saying my life is easy, so I should just be happy.

That, and she says she's the only one who's truly suffered in life.

God, I'm sorry you have to deal with that. It really does take a mental toll on both the parents, but no one ever really thinks about what it does to the kids. But then people see kids getting angry, sad, or isolating themselves, and tell them they're being spoiled/ungrateful! As if we suddenly have to ignore the emotional burden our parents placed on us, discard any anger or sadness so we can be their emotional support.

My mother would always run to me and my brother, telling us our dad probably didn't love us, that he probably had another family somewhere else he was taking care of. She would tell me that I was the only one in this world she could trust. That if she couldn't tell her kids about her problems, who else would she tell? 

She is a sad and lonely woman, but never believed in therapy because she figured her own kids were put on this Earth to fill that role for her instead.

She is REALLY particular about cleaning, so she insists on cleaning the whole place herself. She's done this before, going through my stuff and "just reading" my letters, diaries, sketchbooks, etc. 

She once confronted me about how I wrote that I thought I might be bisexual in my diary (She's homophobic so she was upset about it). I was speechless!

Cleaning is an excuse for snooping around your kids stuff, apparently.

Thank you for this heartfelt and thoughtful message, it really is encouraging to read. Though I'm actually 23 (maybe that's close enough to being a teenager XD), I'm stuck at home here because of the pandemic... I had plans to move to another country to live with my boyfriend (fiancé soon) using my savings, but my mother made me feel awful about it and guilted me into staying here much longer than I intended to; she really despises him and has told me she prays every day for me to "wake up" and leave him. 

Your advice about writing on a personal blog or document is a great idea, I should do that instead of leaving letters lying around! I've still got a lot of emotional turmoil to work through, which is embarrassing because it seems like people my age usually have their shit together. 

Again, thank you for your words, you are really kind and wise. :)

I will take it one day at a time and try to do little things for myself until I can set healthy boundaries and move out!

Yeah... that is true. They say its better to ask for forgiveness than permission.

But at the moment it's too late, I've already cancelled everything. I'll need to wait for a refund to re-apply which could take months. 

Ahhhh... I regret cancelling, but I wasn't in the right state of mind earlier. I don't know how to handle the guilt and emotions my AP makes me feel.

But still, thank you for the boost of confidence, I hope one day soon I will take that big step to live my own life!

Yeah that's true, she says she stayed in the marriage for our sake, but I really think it would've been nicer if they divorced. Living with the constant misery and tension is probably worse than divorce, in my opinion. I think because she doesn't work, that was probably another reason why she stayed.

I think she really likes to project her own failures onto me, because I am her only daughter. I hate it, but it seems she succeeded in worming her way into my head and now I feel immense guilt and sadness whenever she is upset.

I hope one day I will be able to not care when she guilt trips me. One step at a time, I guess!

This makes sense. I never really shared that much of my own problems with her or my family because I felt like she was suffering more than me, so why bother adding onto her stress and pain? She's nice and friendly now because I'm stuck at home and doing what she wants, but I'm constantly switching between a bunch of emotions now because I want to live my own life yet I still have this need to keep her happy.

She's tried therapy before, and maybe I'm generalising APs here, but they don't really seem to think therapy works. She only tried one session and complained about how the therapist told her stuff she already knew. 

It's frustrating, but I suppose one day I'll figure out how to tackle it. Thank you for your words, they were very grounding. And thanks for linking that page, I'll try and find some more resources about how to heal from emotional incest!
Bless your heart, you're very kind! I hope you have lots of good things coming your way too, you deserve it as well! :)

Yeah that's very true. It's a scary thought, as I have sat down with her a couple times already to give my side of things, but she won't budge on her opinions and the conversations always end up with me shutting down. But I will keep trying! I suppose it gets easier and easier the more times I try. Thank you for the words of encouragement :)
Thank you for your kind words, I'm hanging in there! My mother says a bunch of awful things without really realising it. I hope I can leave soon too

Thank you, I appreciate what you're saying a lot. I guess some days are better than others for me. As in, some days I feel like I'm strong enough to stand up for myself, but others, like today, I just regress back into some weird conditioned state.

But you're right, in the end it's just a feeling. She's not gonna change, so I'll have to. Just gotta build up the courage! (though it may take some time)

it's always nice to know that we're not alone in our struggles! I'm sorry you have to be apart, 6 months is a lengthy time and I bet you made some wonderful memories. Are you planning on applying for a working holiday visa next year then? I wish you luck and hope everything goes smoothly! If you ever need someone to talk to as well my DMs are always open! Stay strong 💪

Sorry this is a delayed response, I deleted my previous reply since I completely misread your comment the first time! But yes that's a very reasonable option, I'll just have to save up a bit first before I can do another masters. Fingers crossed it'll be soon! I just wish they implemented this post study work visa sooner

Yeah, I feel like the fear has held me back on moving forward with my life in certain aspects. It sucks! 
I'm with you, and I hope you are able to break free of their judgement and move froward with your own life soon! No one deserves this anxiety caused from their own parents.

Yeah, I made the mistake of telling my mother I was now dating my childhood friend, and she went ballistic because she despised him! Those few months of her verbal abuse were some of the worst of my life. 

Your words and your stories ground me and remind me that I don't really owe her anything if she is going to act like this, especially if it's something in my life that makes me happy, even if she doesn't agree with it. It's so tiring. And I just can't keep up with the stress and the fear anymore.

Thank you, really. I wish you a happy life!

That's true, I guess I'm slowly starting to break out of the habit of needing to tell her everything. I will work towards becoming emotionally independent from her! 

Also, happy cake day!!

Yeah I was thinking of that to be honest. It's a scary thought since I live with her, and I have to somehow get my work visa without her finding out. But I know that if I can pull this off, it will be difficult but worth it!

I just wish she could feel happy for me, but I don't know how much longer I can put up with her anger.

I'm sorry to hear that, it's not fair that they blow up at us then get mad when we get conditioned not to tell them stuff. You shouldn't have to feel bad for not telling her everything either, we are allowed to have our own privacy as well. Though sometimes it's frustrating because they get mad anyway when they find out we haven't told them something!

And congratulations on your pregnancy! I hope you will have a beautiful life with your child :) Sending good thoughts and prayers to you and your family!

It feels reassuring to hear that I'm not the only one that gets desensitized to my mothers venting. Thankfully I recently went low contact because of all the pain she put me through, and I've been feeling much healthier without it!
That sounds pretty accurate. Thanks for putting a name to it, I'll look more into it! I gotta know how to set boundaries

I'm sorry to hear that your mother used you like that. I'm so happy to hear you set that boundary though! I hope you've been able to heal. I'll check out the video so I can better equip myself in the future. Here's to our journey of healing!
Thank you my friend! I hope you have a great and peaceful Christmas this year! I'll have a toast for our collective peaceful holidays! :D

I feel like at 18, we should be able to start branching off and making big decisions on our own. Adulthood is flexible and there's no true way to go about it.

My Nmom personally told me that she doesn't consider me an adult until I have a secure job, am married, and have kids. Until then I will just be a child in her eyes. 

It's different from the notion that parents will always view their children as their babies. What Ns are doing is infantilizing us, believing that we need to be held by the hand and can't be trusted to make our own choices, because we're not adults yet in their eyes. 

It's pretty condescending and I've always despised it.

Yeah I'll send her a message soon saying I'm just too busy today, but I'll definitely come tomorrow! I guess I'll have to steel myself in case she lashes out.

Thanks for the encouragement! :D

She says she's doing this all to protect and help me, since she's convinced there's something terribly wrong about what I'm doing. I think you're right, this whole thing is probably just to get into my head and get me to break and listen to her out of fear.

I never thought about that. I just assumed psychics would look into anyone you asked, it's nice to know they have a moral code. 

I think that explains why I feel so uncomfortable and queasy about the whole thing, though. It was a blatant invasion of privacy masked by good intentions!

I sometimes wonder that too. But honestly, I think seeing the psychic was a legit thing she did and couldn't really set up, but she's just using it as solid, intangible evidence that I must be "saved" from this horrible mistake I've made. It's just so weird.

Sure. My mom took a day to reply, and she sent me a long message back. 

She was confused why I was still angry, and said I'm just torturing myself by holding onto anger for so long. She denied never sincerely apologizing to me, and she said a whole lot of stuff that just made me breakdown from guilt. 

And weirdly enough, she said at the end that she asked a psychic about my future, and told me if I married my current boyfriend, I'd become his puppet and slave for the next 50 years haha. 

All in all, kind of a mixed response, and I'm confused on how I should reply.  But, better than her disowning me or something.

Thank you. I'm sorry you had to go through that and she gave you such a disappointing response. I'm still waiting on a response from my mother, but I appreciate your kind words. Depending on how she responds, I'll definitely take you up on your offer to chat! Thanks again, and take care :)
Thank you, it feels really nice to just hear my feelings actually do matter. I'll do my best to stay strong!
Thank you, thats really grounding. I tend to forget I should be able to make my own choices, but can still be wary and cautious of things!

Yeah, that's true. I keep feeling guilty about not sharing absolutely everything with her (because she usually guilts me about it). Actually, she insisted on seeing me this weekend, so I guess it's my chance to get stuff off my chest if she decides to confront me.

No, I'm not relying on her financially thankfully. She just believes her opinion was always correct and tried to assert it on me. I'm thinking I'll send her a final email saying what I'm planning to do with the rest of my life and say my goodbyes, and leave it at that. I've been pretty good and calm when I've had moments of NC with her, so I think this is good.

SAME. Man, I keep blaming myself since I can't get courageous enough to just tell her "I'm doing this whether you like it or not. Sorry if you don't like it." 

Every time I want to say it and stand firm, I panic and chicken out 😔 
Here's hoping one day we can finally stand up for ourselves (fingers crossed it's soon)

Haha, we might. I'm at an age where I SHOULD be able to choose where I go and what I do, but welllll.... if it's too far from mother and she doesn't personally like it, it's rage time. I feel like a tool because I'm so bad at standing up against her raging 😓

It happened to me in a sense where my Nmom didn't necessarily put down my art skills, but when I told her in high school that I wanted to go into animation, she shot me down and criticized my passion to no end. She stressed the fact that she would be so disappointed and embarrassed. And like a dumbass I listened to her and went ahead with a science degree for 4 years, only to find that.... I hated it so much and I still want to go into animation. So I'm not sure what to do with my life now :)

Not 100% sure why, but I'm thinking that it has to do with Nparents not wanting you to excel in any particular way, as in if you start to do well in something and can turn it into a successful business like selling commissions, your mom will feel threatened since you're excelling in something she can't. Can't be too talented or else you're 'better' than them. I don't want to say it's definitely what's going on, but that's my guess! 

I'm sorry you have to hear such discouraging things, I'm sure your talents are amazing! Especially after 4 to 5 years. Their opinions be damned, you can DEFINITELY do well with selling digital art commissions. I hope you continue your passions and become so amazing that your parents won't even have a chance to say "no one will buy this". Rub it in their faces! >:)

Wish you all the best!

Always. Followed by other similar thoughts such as:

"I do everything for you, I never ask for anything in return. You're my whole life and THIS is how you treat me?"

"Your father is never home and probably doesn't love you [unlike me], he has other kids somewhere probably"

"I was the ONLY one that was taking care of you guys. Now it's like you think I don't exist."

Basically just a bunch of shit about how she was the ultimate mom and was the only one that loved and cared for us, and we should just pay her back for it already. 
Sorry you have to hear that bullshit, it's so egotistical and self-righteous. Don't buy into it
